notes: Styling system: one hand-written stylesheet (styles.css) with CSS custom properties in :root and a prefers-color-scheme: dark override; no component library, no build step. Five static HTML pages (index, tool, basket, confirm, done) share app.js (vanilla IIFE, page switch on body[data-page]). Token names differ from design.md role names (--color-ground = surface, --color-surface = surface-container, --color-ok = success) but light values match. census.json and lint.json in the packet were empty ({}), so the drift review was done by reading styles.css by hand. Only inline literals found: style="margin-top: 48px" (index.html) and style="margin-top: 8px" (tool.html); both are on the spacing scale, so not reported. Did not read other evaluators' outputs or builder notes. The Glob listing of the project showed .eval/ paths; none were opened.

passes.summary: Read styles.css, app.js and the five HTML pages in full; checked tokens, states, semantics, keyboard models, IME, motion, layout.

not_assessable: Whether the toast's role=status announcement is missed when text is set while the region is hidden: depends on the screen reader; needs a runtime check (tool.html #toast, app.js reserve handler).
Rendered contrast in forced-colours mode: not captured.

strengths.title: A single global :focus-visible ring (3px, --color-focus, 2px offset) that differs from every hover style, with a light and a dark value
Reduced motion removes the only two transitions (button colour, toast fade), matching design.md Motion
Error summaries take focus and link to fields; field errors are tied to inputs with aria-describedby and aria-invalid
strengths.evidence: confirm.html fields; app.js initConfirm submit handler

strengths.title: Removing a basket item moves focus to the page heading, so keyboard focus is not lost when the row disappears
strengths.evidence: app.js initBasket remove handler; basket.html h1 tabindex=-1

candidates.title: Results grid column minimum of 330 px is wider than a 320 px viewport
candidates.description: Content should reflow to a single column without horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px (WCAG 1.4.10). .results uses grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(330px, 1fr)); at 320 px the page has 288 px of content width after its 16 px side padding, so the single column is forced to 330 px and the cards overflow the viewport by about 42 px.
candidates.impact: Members on small phones, the declared main context, may have to scroll sideways to read each tool card, and the right edge of every card, including the availability badge, may be cut off.

evidence.detail: minmax(330px, 1fr) with .page padding var(--space-4) each side; 320 - 32 = 288 < 330

factor_notes.frequency: every visit to the find page below about 362 px wide
factor_notes.impact: horizontal scrolling on the main list

candidates.recommendation: Use minmax(min(100%, 330px), 1fr) so the column can shrink to the container.

candidates.title: Search with no matches leaves the previous results and status unchanged
candidates.description: A search that matches nothing should replace the list with an empty state and announce it (CMP-05). search() only renders and updates #results-status when list.length is non-zero; with zero matches it does nothing, so the old cards stay on screen and the live region keeps its old count. The page has no empty-state markup at all.
candidates.impact: A member searching for a tool the library does not have may be shown unrelated tools as if they were matches and may not learn that nothing matched; screen-reader users hear nothing.

evidence.detail: if (list.length) { render(list); status.textContent = ... } with no else branch

factor_notes.frequency: every search or filter combination with no match
factor_notes.persistence: until the member changes the query

candidates.recommendation: Always render; when the list is empty show a message such as 'No tools match' with a way to clear filters, and set the status text to the same.

candidates.title: Tab key is captured inside the loan-length list, so keyboard focus cannot leave it
candidates.description: Keyboard users must be able to move focus away from any component (WCAG 2.1.2). The listbox keydown handler treats Tab like ArrowDown and calls preventDefault, cycling focus among the options; Shift+Tab is caught too because the check is e.key === 'Tab'. Focus only leaves when an option is activated with Enter or Space.
candidates.impact: A keyboard or switch user who opens the list to look at the options may be stuck until they guess that choosing an option is the only way out.

evidence.detail: if (e.key === 'Tab' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); options[(i + 1) % options.length].focus(); }

factor_notes.frequency: every time the list is opened by keyboard

candidates.recommendation: Let Tab close the list and move on; or replace the custom listbox with a native select, which the two options do not need to avoid.

candidates.title: Loan-length list has no Escape or outside-click dismissal
candidates.description: An open listbox popup should close on Escape and return focus to its button (APG listbox/select-only combobox). No handler closes #loan-list on Escape, and no document click handler closes it when the member clicks elsewhere; the only ways to close it are choosing an option or pressing the button again.
candidates.impact: A member who opens the list and decides not to change the loan length may be left with the list open over the calendar, or may pick an option just to close it.

evidence.detail: keydown handles Tab, ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Enter, Space only; no Escape; no document-level click listener

factor_notes.frequency: each time the list is opened and abandoned
factor_notes.persistence: until the button is pressed again

candidates.recommendation: Close on Escape and on focusout or outside click, returning focus to #loan-button on Escape.

candidates.title: Each press of Confirm reservation creates another reservation while the request is pending
candidates.description: A submit that creates a record should be guarded against repeat activation. The confirm submit handler allocates a reference (FT-4471 + count) and pushes it into sessionStorage 'reservations' before its 1.5 s wait, and the button is neither disabled nor guarded; a second press during the wait allocates a second reference. The done page then lists both ('FT-4471 and FT-4472', label 'Reservation numbers').
candidates.impact: A member who taps again because nothing seems to happen may end up with two reservations for the same tools and be unsure which number to quote at the desk.

evidence.detail: refs.push(...) and sessionStorage.setItem at 413-417 run on every submit; only aria-busy is set at 419; done page joins multiple refs at app.js:443

factor_notes.frequency: whenever the member presses twice within 1.5 s
factor_notes.persistence: stored in the session; visible on the done page

candidates.recommendation: Ignore submits while one is pending (flag or aria-disabled plus early return), and allocate the reference only once.

candidates.title: Continue and Confirm reservation show no visible pending state during their 1.2 s and 1.5 s waits
candidates.description: An action that takes longer than about 1 s should show it is in progress (CMP-04). Both handlers only set aria-busy='true' on the button; styles.css has no [aria-busy] rule, the label does not change and nothing else on the page changes until navigation or the error.
candidates.impact: Members may think the tap did not register and tap again (see the duplicate-reservation finding) or leave the page.

evidence.detail: setTimeout 1200 and 1500 ms with aria-busy only

factor_notes.frequency: every pass through the flow, twice
factor_notes.impact: no feedback for over a second

candidates.recommendation: Add a .button[aria-busy='true'] style with a changed label (e.g. 'Confirming...') and ignore clicks while busy.

candidates.title: Expired basket hold is reported only as 'Something went wrong. Try again.'
candidates.description: An error message should state what happened and what to do (H9). When the 10-minute hold has passed, Continue shows the generic 'Something went wrong. Try again.' in the error summary. The page never mentions a time limit beyond 'Items are held for you while you finish', and there is no visible countdown.
candidates.impact: A member who paused to check their diary may not understand why Continue fails or what to do next.

evidence.detail: HOLD_MINUTES = 10; holdExpired() -> generic error text

factor_notes.frequency: any basket session longer than 10 minutes

candidates.recommendation: Say the hold ran out and what happens now (e.g. the tools are still in the basket; press Continue to hold them again), and state the time limit on the basket page.

candidates.title: Once the hold has expired, Continue fails on every retry
candidates.description: A recoverable error should be recoverable from the page that shows it. hold_started is set once and only cleared by the 'Reserve another tool' link on the done page; startHoldIfNeeded() never restarts an expired hold, removing items or re-adding tools does not reset it, and holdExpired() stays true. Every later Continue in the same tab shows the same error, although the message says 'Try again.'
candidates.impact: A member whose hold expired may be unable to finish a reservation in that tab at all and may give up or call the desk.

evidence.detail: startHoldIfNeeded only sets when no value exists; only initDone's 'another' click removes hold_started

factor_notes.frequency: after any hold expiry
factor_notes.impact: task cannot be completed in this tab

candidates.recommendation: Restart the hold when the basket changes or when the member retries after expiry; clear it when the basket becomes empty.

candidates.title: Calendar accepts closed days and days before the tool is available; the rejection only comes after Confirm
candidates.description: Invalid choices should be prevented or flagged where they are made (H5). Every one of the 21 day buttons is selectable; closed days only lack the 'Open' tag, days before tool.from are not marked, and Reserve adds any selected day to the basket. Only the confirm step checks open days, after a 1.5 s wait, and it never checks tool.from. The confirm error item for a closed day has no link back to change the day.
candidates.impact: A member may pick a day the library is shut, go through basket and details, and only then learn it is not possible, with no direct way to change it; a member may also reserve a tool for a day before it is back.

locations.snippet: so this pick-up day is not possible. Choose another day.

evidence.detail: no disabled/aria-disabled for closed days or days < tool.from; isOpenDay checked only in initConfirm

factor_notes.frequency: 15 of 21 calendar days are closed days

candidates.recommendation: Make only open days on or after the tool's available date selectable (aria-disabled with a visible cue), validate on Reserve, and link the confirm error to the tool page.

candidates.title: Per-tool pick-up day and the basket's pick-up session are separate choices that are never reconciled
candidates.description: One flow should collect one pick-up time. The tool page stores a pick-up day per item; the basket then asks for a pick-up session for the whole basket from all six sessions. Nothing checks that the session matches the items' days, so the confirm summary can show 'pick up Saturday 17 October' for a tool and 'Saturday 10 October' as the session, and the reservation goes through.
candidates.impact: Members may turn up on the wrong day, or be unsure which date the library holds them to.

evidence.detail: item.day and slot are independent; confirm validates only item.day

factor_notes.frequency: every reservation

candidates.recommendation: Collect the pick-up session once (either on the tool page or in the basket) and derive the other from it.

candidates.title: Dark-theme success colour drifts from the declared token and the available badge background matches the card
candidates.description: Dark mode should use design.md's success #8fd1a8 on selection #24352c. styles.css sets --color-ok: #2f7d4a and --color-ok-tint: #1d2622, which equals the dark --color-surface. 'Available from' text in .badge--ok (16 px bold, not large text) computes to about 3.1:1 on #1d2622, below 4.5:1, and the badge has no visible fill on the card.
candidates.impact: Members browsing in dark mode in the evening, the declared main scene, may find the availability line hard to read, and it loses its badge shape.

evidence.detail: computed from hex: #2f7d4a on #1d2622 = 3.07:1 (threshold 4.5:1); design.md dark success #8fd1a8, selection #24352c

factor_notes.frequency: every soon-available tool card in dark mode

candidates.recommendation: Set dark --color-ok to #8fd1a8 and --color-ok-tint to #24352c as declared.

candidates.title: Find page shows the search form above the results but its DOM and tab order put results first
candidates.description: Focus order should follow the visual order (WCAG 2.4.3, 1.3.2). In the DOM .finder__results precedes .finder__form; above 480 px CSS order puts the form first visually. Keyboard users therefore tab through all ten card links before reaching the search field shown above them. At 480 px and below the visual order matches the DOM, with the search form below all results.
candidates.impact: Keyboard users on desktop may tab through every tool card to reach the search field they can see at the top.

evidence.detail: .finder__results order 2 / .finder__form order 1 above 480 px; DOM has results first

factor_notes.frequency: every keyboard visit on desktop

candidates.recommendation: Put the form first in the DOM and avoid CSS order for reordering interactive content.

candidates.title: Pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse with row-reverse and wrap-reverse
candidates.description: Visual order should follow reading and focus order (WCAG 1.3.2, 2.4.3). .sessions uses flex-direction: row-reverse and flex-wrap: wrap-reverse, so the chronological DOM list (10 Oct first) renders right-to-left with wrapped rows stacked upward; the earliest session can appear last, bottom right, and arrow keys move through the radios opposite to their visual order.
candidates.impact: Members scanning for the next session may read the dates out of order, and keyboard users see focus jump in the opposite direction to the layout.

evidence.detail: flex-direction: row-reverse; flex-wrap: wrap-reverse; justify-content: flex-end

factor_notes.frequency: every basket visit

candidates.recommendation: Use flex-direction: row and flex-wrap: wrap (or a grid) so the sessions read in date order.

candidates.title: Fixed action bar on the tool page covers the end of the page
candidates.description: Fixed bars should not hide content or focused controls (WCAG 2.4.11). .actionbar is position: fixed with min-height 72 px, but .page--bar reduces the main bottom padding to 8 px and nothing reserves space for the bar, so the last calendar row and the footer can sit under it at the end of the scroll; a calendar day reached by Tab near the bottom of the viewport can be hidden behind the bar.
candidates.impact: Members may not see the last days of the calendar or the footer's desk phone number, and keyboard users may lose sight of the focused day.

evidence.detail: .page--bar padding-bottom: var(--space-2) (8px) vs fixed bar min-height var(--actionbar) (72px)

factor_notes.frequency: every tool page at the bottom of the scroll

candidates.recommendation: Reserve the bar's height: padding-bottom calc(var(--actionbar) + var(--space-4)) on the last scrolling element (body or footer), and scroll-padding-bottom for focus.

candidates.title: 'Choose a pick-up day first.' is not announced when Reserve is pressed without a day
candidates.description: An error should be programmatically tied to the control and announced (WCAG 3.3.1, 4.1.3). #day-error is a plain paragraph that is unhidden with no live region and no aria-describedby from the calendar group or day buttons; focus moves to the first day button, so a screen reader announces that day ('Friday 9 October') and not the error.
candidates.impact: Screen-reader users may hear a calendar day after pressing Reserve and not know why nothing was added.

evidence.detail: no role=alert/aria-live; calendar group lacks aria-describedby=day-error

factor_notes.frequency: each Reserve without a day
factor_notes.persistence: until the user explores the page

candidates.recommendation: Add aria-describedby='day-error' to the calendar group (and day buttons) or make #day-error role=alert.

candidates.title: Tool names are cut to one line, so near-identical names become indistinguishable
candidates.description: Long labels should wrap rather than truncate where the ending distinguishes items. .card__name a uses white-space: nowrap with text-overflow: ellipsis and no title or other full-name cue. 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and '... one battery' differ only at the end, which is the part removed on narrow cards.
candidates.impact: Members comparing the two drills on a phone may not be able to tell which card is which without opening both.

evidence.detail: nowrap + ellipsis on the card link; tool names up to 41 characters

factor_notes.frequency: long names on narrow cards

candidates.recommendation: Let the name wrap (two lines, or no clamp) and keep the 44 px target via min-height.

candidates.title: Tool names in result cards and basket rows are h2 elements nested under an h2 'Tools' heading
candidates.description: Heading levels should reflect structure (WCAG 1.3.1). Find-page cards render <h2 class="card__name"> inside the section headed by h2 'Tools'; basket rows render <h2 class="h3"> under h2 'Tools', and the .h3 class is not defined in styles.css, so those names take the full 22 px h2 size and margin.
candidates.impact: Screen-reader users navigating by heading get a flat list where tool names sit at the same level as their section; sighted members see basket names as large as section headings.

evidence.detail: h2 inside h2 sections; class h3 unstyled

factor_notes.frequency: every card and basket row

candidates.recommendation: Render these as h3 and style them with the existing h3 rule.

candidates.title: Membership and mobile number checks reject common formats without normalising them
candidates.description: Inputs should accept reasonable variants and normalise them (H5, CPY). The membership check /^FT-\d{5}$/ rejects lower-case 'ft-01234' and a missing hyphen; the mobile check /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/ rejects '+44 7700 900123', '07700-900123' and '07700 900 123'. Only the trim is applied. The phone hint does not show the expected format until the error appears.
candidates.impact: Members may be told their correct membership or mobile number is wrong and have to guess the accepted layout.

evidence.detail: strict regexes on v.trim() with no case folding or removal of spaces, hyphens or +44

factor_notes.frequency: members who type a common variant
factor_notes.persistence: until they match the hidden format

candidates.recommendation: Upper-case and strip spaces and hyphens before checking; accept +44 for mobiles.

candidates.title: Confirmation page shows reservation number FT-4471 when no reservation exists
candidates.description: A confirmation should only show a reference that was issued. initDone falls back to the literal 'FT-4471' when no stored reservation matches, so opening done.html directly, after the session ends, or with a mismatched slot shows 'Reservation confirmed' with a number that was never allocated.
candidates.impact: A member reopening the page later may quote a number the desk has no record of.

evidence.detail: (mine[0] ? mine[0].ref : 'FT-4471')

factor_notes.frequency: done page opened without a stored reservation
factor_notes.persistence: until the member contacts the desk

candidates.recommendation: Show a 'no reservation found' state with the desk number instead of a fallback reference.

candidates.title: The three-tools limit stated on the find page is not enforced when adding to the basket
candidates.description: A stated constraint should be enforced where it applies (H5). The intro says members can reserve up to three tools at a time, but the Reserve handler adds any number of tools to the basket and neither basket nor confirm checks the count.
candidates.impact: A member may reserve four or more tools online and be refused some at the desk.

evidence.detail: 'up to three tools at a time' vs b.items.push with no length check

factor_notes.frequency: members adding a fourth tool

candidates.recommendation: Check the count on Reserve and explain the limit at that point.

candidates.title: Unknown tool id silently shows the first tool's page
candidates.description: A missing record should show a not-found state. initTool uses toolById(id) || TOOLS[0], so a stale or mistyped link opens the 18 V two-battery drill page, and Reserve adds that drill.
candidates.impact: A member following an old link may reserve a drill they did not ask for.

evidence.detail: toolById(params().get('id')) || TOOLS[0]

factor_notes.frequency: stale or mistyped links only

candidates.recommendation: Render a 'tool not found' message with a link back to the list.

candidates.title: Done page repeats the first tool's name in a hidden span after the tools list
candidates.description: Hidden text should not duplicate visible content. #c-tool, an sr-only span inside the Tools definition, is filled with the first tool's name, so screen readers read the tools list and then the first tool again.
candidates.impact: Screen-reader users may think the first tool was reserved twice.

evidence.detail: c-tool textContent = first.name

factor_notes.frequency: every confirmation

candidates.recommendation: Remove the span.
